name: Ricky Skaggs
notes: Two parameter sets in one career: the neotraditional country run whose 1990s tail is modelled here, and the 1996-onward return to bluegrass with Kentucky Thunder, which the entry calls the section's canonical drummerless train-beat lane. `bpm` spans both stated bands — 90–160 for the country lane and 150–210 for the bluegrass one. The section states the rule this whole wing turns on: "the train beat is an ensemble function, not a drum part" — the banjo roll carries the continuous subdivision, the mandolin chop supplies the backbeat, and the upright bass supplies the two-beat kick. This entry is where the section states it, so the drum block is the ensemble reading rather than a kit: the inherited `train_16ths` stream stands for the banjo roll, `velocityTiers` are compressed to brush range (accent 84–100 against ghost 40–56) because "where drums appear ... they are a straight 8th stream with brushes and a two-beat kick", the hat is on quarters and not continuous, and `percs` is two quiet lanes at −10 dB. `snare.offGridMs` −6 is the grammar block's anticipated feel — "notes are anticipated, in contrast to laid-back blues where notes are behind the beat" — pushed further here than in the radio wing because the chop is the backbeat. Keys are the stated G/A/B♭/D with capo transposition; harmony is the sourced bluegrass convention, I–IV–V as the spine with I–♭VII–IV mixolydian borrows and Dorian/Mixolydian colour on the mountain repertoire, which is why `extensions.triad` is 0.86 — the plainest harmony of this wing. The bass is the sourced "rhythmic alternation between the root and fifth of each chord, with occasional walking bass excursions", i.e. a loosened `followRootsProb` and a high `anticipationProb` for the slap-style accent and the ahead-of-grid placement. ⚠ INFERRED: the velocity tiers, the −6 ms offset value, `percs` contents and every melody and countermelody number. ⚠ The entry is explicit that "readings are sparse — only the slow end of his catalogue is in the database, so the fast band is inferred from the bluegrass-breakdown convention and marked [LOW-CONF]"; `bpm.mode` 170 carries that flag. It rates itself medium-high on grammar and era split, medium-low on tempo.
